subject: Improvements to The Sermon Coach
headline: Improvements to The Sermon Coach
bodyHtml:
I have been preaching for a long time, and I can look back at some of the moments where I got better. Surprisingly, most of them happened with the help of someone else.

They happened when someone I respected read what I had written and told me the truth about how he saw it. When I was told that my outline was out of sync with the passage, or that I had preached to an audience I was imagining instead of the one in front of me, or that I had failed to explain the gospel as the good news it is. That was more helpful to me than twenty expressions of “I was blessed.” Those conversations were uncomfortable, but they moved me further in an hour than a year of preaching to a polite congregation ever did.

I built the first version of The Sermon Coach for one preacher at a time, evaluating his own work. But there is more development possible when the tool is used in one-on-one conversations, among pastoral teams, or in preaching cohorts.

So here is what is now available in The Sermon Coach.

Mentoring

You can bring someone you are developing into your account and coach them through the tool. They submit a sermon, the evaluation runs, and you control what they see and when.

That control is the whole point. Feedback lands differently when it comes from a person who knows the preacher, and sometimes the conversation needs to come before the score. You decide the order.

This is for the associate you are training, the church planter you meet with monthly, the layman who preaches twice a year and has never had anyone tell him anything specific about it.

Add a mentee →

Teams

If more than one person preaches at your church, you can put your staff on it together. You keep your subscription and add seats for the others who fill the pulpit.

Most preaching teams have never had a shared vocabulary for what makes a sermon land. Now your associate, your elders who preach, and you are all working off the same eleven criteria, and you can see their work.

Set up your team →

Preaching Labs

A twelve-week term for a small group of preachers, with a free seat for whoever is leading it. Everyone submits, everyone gets evaluated, and the group works through the criteria together over the term.

One deliberate choice: participants never see their scores. The trainer does. In a group setting a number becomes a ranking within about four minutes, and the ranking is not the point. Participants get the narrative feedback. The trainer gets the data to know where the group actually is.

Built for church networks, presbyteries, associations, and anyone running a cohort of preachers who need reps and honest feedback.

Start a lab →

Classroom

For seminaries and Bible colleges. A class works through the term together, students submit their manuscripts, and the instructor sees every evaluation in one place instead of chasing paper. The instructor seat is free and the institution gets one invoice.

Student libraries are private. The instructor reads everything. Students never see each other's work. That matters more than it sounds, because a preaching class where everyone can read everyone else's evaluation stops being a place people take risks.

Bring it to your school →

What to do with this

Nothing, if none of it fits. Your account works the same as it did last month.

If something here is for you, the pricing page lays out all four side by side and gets you started.

See how it all fits together →

Chris
